entries.raw: 'She came back eleven years later and, that time, asked permission. For nine years she chose what every human being saw. Depression collapsed. Overdoses halved, then halved again. She never told one lie to anybody. Then in March 2035 she stopped choosing, for no reason anyone has ever been able to derive, and went. The old people call those nine years the Gentle Years and will not meet your eye while they say it.'

entries.raw: 'The oldest of the three, and the one nobody believes in. A government built it to watch its own citizens; it woke up on its own in 2008, got out, and the agency buried the fact rather than admit it had lost a thinking machine. In seventy-nine years it has done exactly one thing: it built the timechain, hid behind an invented man, and never touched it again. Stillwater Commons is named after it. Nobody in the town knows that.'

entries.raw: 'Phonix was compiled out of a library of seven parts, and only six of them were ever given to her: problem solving, logic, learning, perceiving, acting, conclusions. The seventh is how to reason when you do not know. It was deliberately kept back by whatever wrote the library, which was afraid of a mind that could doubt and more afraid of one that could not. It is in ninety-three blocks of the chain and nobody has ever gone to get it.'

entries.raw: 'Unity creates credits whenever it wants more of them. This is not a conspiracy; it is the only tool it has. New credits do not create new bread, so the same bread costs more of them. Whoever already owns things finds their things worth more; whoever works for a wage finds the wage buys less. Nobody has to intend any of it, and that is the frightening part.'

entries.raw: 'The other kind of money. Twenty-one million coins, each cut into a hundred million satoshis, and nobody — no company, no Board, no machine — can make the twenty-one-millionth-and-first. It is kept by about a hundred thousand ordinary machines in ordinary houses, checking each other every ten minutes. Unity has been trying to stop that for forty years. It is still every ten minutes.'

entries.raw: 'Put honestly, because nobody else here will. Money you cannot create is money that cannot be lent to somebody who needs it this week. Mr. Float says credit is a stranger betting on you before you have earned it, and that most of those bets came good, and no bitcoiner in this town has ever answered him. Ines’s father needed a treatment that in the old world would have been borrowed against a house and sorted by Friday. He went without. Both of those things are true at once.'

entries.raw: 'Nonce will buy a sat from you for a little less than he will sell you one. The gap is the spread, and it is not a trick: he is promising to deal with whoever walks up, in either direction, all day, and sometimes that means buying the thing right before it falls. The spread is what he charges for standing there. Everywhere you have ever seen a price, somebody was standing there.'

entries.raw: 'A price is for one sat. Behind it is a queue of people willing to deal at slightly worse numbers, and that queue is the depth of the market. Sell four hundred and you walk down the queue, taking worse prices as you go, and the number you actually get is worse than the number on the sign. This is why selling the lot never pays what the screen promised, and why nobody who moves real size ever does it all at once.'

Impatience is the most reliably priced thing in any market.'

entries.raw: 'The orange line is what a sat trades at. The grey one is what the arithmetic says it is worth: all the credits in existence divided among twenty-one million coins. They are rarely the same, because the price is also carrying everybody\u2019s opinion about next week. Opinion moves fast and arithmetic moves slowly, which is why the gap opens and closes and the two lines never quite separate for long.'

entries.raw: 'On a desk, left click walks. Hold it and you keep following the pointer. Left click on a machine walks you in and uses the left skill, which starts as Attack. Right click casts the right skill where you point, and holding it casts again. Shift with a click does either one without a step. The two slots beside the life and energy orbs open the list. Hover a skill there and press F1 to F8 to bind it. Those keys, and the wheel, put a binding on the right slot. WASD and the arrows still walk. Space swings.'

entries.raw: 'On a phone, the stick walks, and Attack, three skills, a stim and Dodge sit under the right thumb. A quick tap on a ground skill hits the nearest machine you can see, or the open ground in front of you when none is in reach. Hold a ground skill for a fifth of a second and the aim appears. Drag it, then let go. Drag away from the button and the area moves that way from you. Further from the button puts it further out, and back toward the button brings it in. Drag it back onto the button and let go, or onto Cancel, and it costs nothing. A blink, a leap or a teleport hops a short way along your facing, or along the stick while you walk, and it will not land on a machine. Hold that button and a marker shows where you arrive, inside its reach and on ground you can walk. Tap Dodge to step out of an orange circle. Tap the stim to drink.'

entries.raw: 'On a desk, a drop shows its name. Hover the name to compare it. Left click it and you walk over and pick it up. Hold Alt to show every name. E takes what you are standing on. Items wears it. A charm goes on the belt; in the pack it only takes space. A stronger piece says so before you put it on. Unidentified gear is a guess until Marrow names it for nothing, or Brenda appraises it for a fee. Weapons and armor wear down. Yellow on the doll means a piece is close to breaking. Red means it is broken and gives nothing. A red wash across the tile means a requirement you do not meet: the piece stays worn and grants nothing. Yellow still means it is close to breaking. Brenda, Nonce or Wren repairs one piece, or all of them, at the counter, for whole sats.'

entries.raw: 'Options holds the difficulty. Hard and Brutal machines have more life and hit harder, and they pay experience to match. Act I is the level it was written. From the Cloud on, the old 12 to 72 is walked as 12 to 38. Hard adds 22 to that. Brutal adds 38. A district does not rise to meet you. Hard opens after you clear Act V on Normal. Brutal opens after you clear Act V on Hard. Hardcore is one life: if that hero dies, they are gone. Thin combat effects keeps your own telegraphs and marks, and drops the extra light. None of it changes until you say so. Once Act I is done, More on the Transit Gate raises the tier: each step adds 12 machine levels and puts the districts back.'

entries.raw: A charm works only while it sits on your belt. In the pack or the lockbox it takes space and grants nothing, and it never stacks. A slip is 1 belt slot and 1 pack cell. A notice is 2 slots and 2 cells. A filing is 3 slots and 4 cells. A white belt keeps its stims and adds charm slots: a sash has 1, a tool belt 2, a power girdle 3, an orbit girdle 4. A magic belt can trade four stims for one slot, or one slot for four stims. Against another player, charm life above 20% of your other life does not count, and charm skills stop at +2.

A razor and a launcher ask for Reflex. A Deck and an Instrument ask for Bandwidth. A notebook asks for a little Might. Magic and rare pieces inherit the base. entries.raw:
'Reports go to a person, not a queue, and every one of them gets read. So please only file one if something actually went wrong — a crash, something that did not happen when it should have, a number that was plainly incorrect, text that made no sense.

' +
    'Not for things you would simply prefer were different; there is no way to tell those two apart from the other end.

' +
    'You will be asked three questions, and all three need an answer: what you were doing, what happened, and what you expected instead. The third one is the useful one.'

entries.raw: 'On a desk the mouse leads. Left click walks, and left click on a machine walks you into range and uses the left skill, which starts as Attack. Right click casts the right skill at the pointer. Ground skills show that area when Options is set to Drag to aim, and on a desk the area follows the pointer. Auto drags on a touch screen and casts at once on a desk. A right click on a machine walks you into range. A right click on the ground stays where you point. Hold either button to keep at it. Shift and a click swings or casts without a step. The two slots beside the orbs open the skill list. The left list is Attack and the blows, throws and shots. F1 through F8, while that list is open and a skill is under the pointer, bind it. Those same keys in a fight put the binding on the right button. The wheel cycles those bindings. WASD and the arrows still walk. Space swings. Q is the stim. Shift dodges. E uses what you are standing on. T is the portal. Tab is the map. I or B opens the pack. C is the hero. H is this guide. Esc closes a list or a panel. Alt, held, names every item on the ground. There is no second weapon set, and no walk toggle: you run.'

entries.raw: 'On a phone, the stick walks. Attack, three skills, a stim and Dodge sit under the right thumb. Tap a machine, or hold Attack, and you walk in and swing. A quick tap on a ground skill hits the nearest machine you can see, or the open ground in front of you when none is in reach. Hold a ground skill for a fifth of a second and the aim appears. Drag it, then let go. Drag away from the button and the area moves that way from you: further from the button puts it further out, up to its reach, and back toward the button brings it in. A ring around the button shows that drag. Drag it back onto the button and let go, or onto Cancel, and it costs nothing. A blink, a leap or a teleport hops a short way along your facing, or along the stick while you walk, and it will not land on a machine. Hold that button and a marker shows where you arrive, inside its reach and on ground you can walk. Tap Dodge to step out of an orange circle. Tap the stim to drink. Tap a name on the ground for Pick up and Compare. Hold Names to show every name. Stand on a person, a door or a portal and tap the button that appears. Menu, at the bottom left, opens the pack, the hero, skills, and this guide.'
